posts.caption:
Few drinks convey sunny elegance quite like a Spritz. Our Riviera variation begins with a remarkable strawberry amaro crafted from North Fork Strawberry Wine, along with eau de vie, whose gentle bitterness is complemented by nectarine, grapefruit, and prosecco. 

Equal parts refreshing and sophisticated, this is the sort of cocktail best enjoyed slowly on a warm evening in Manhattan.
Settle in at ZZ’s Brasserie, order the Sushi Platter, and leave it to us to make Toyosu Market’s finest absolutely shine.
Now playing at the bar in Miami: The Tokyo Rickey, which takes the classic highball — traditionally made with citrus, sugar, and the bartender’s spirit of choice – on a trip to Japan.
The Bento Box that dreams are made of, starring the ZZ’s Salmon Avocado Roll. Available exclusively at lunch.

At Carbone Privato, the fleeting beauty of peak-season tomatoes finds expression in the beloved Carbone Caprese, featuring Cherry, Sun Gold, and Demi-Sec Tomatoes, along with House Mozzarella, Salsa Verde, and Thai and Opal Basil.

For two epic nights, Bar Leone brought the World’s Best Bar to ZZ’s. Thank you again to lorenzoantinori_, @sanpellegrino_official, @diageo, and all of our Members for making it one for the record books!
A modern riff on the margarita, The Infante blends blanco tequila, lime, macadamia, orgeat, and orange flower water—finished with a coconut salt rim. Bright, buttery, and made for spring in New York.
A sign that stands for the best night in Miami. Welcome to ZZ’s.

Dear Members, 
We had a night last night. Let’s do it one more time. Before they go back across the world, don’t miss the final night of the WORLD’S BEST BAR, @barleonehk by @lorenzoantinori_, tonight at ZZ’s.

The Matcha Margarita is one of those drinks that tends to attract repeat visits — especially in summer. Combining blanco tequila, fresh lime, and ceremonial-grade matcha, it remains a perennial favorite among Members in both New York and Miami.
latest_comments: Best matcha cocktail I’ve ever had!!! 💚

posts.caption:
The Daiquiri may be one of the world’s most perfect cocktails, but summertime invites a little improvisation. 

This seasonal variation showcases the concentrated sweetness of seedless watermelon, paired with Mount Gay Rum from Barbados, fresh lime, Thai basil, and a hint of vanilla. The result is impossible to resist on a sunny afternoon in the Magic City.
Some Sundays are better than others. This one belongs to Mom. Sadelle’s brunch returns to ZZ’s New York.
Experience the delicacy of soft shell crab in all its glory. A decadent tempura Spider Roll dressed with shiso, scallion, and wasabi mayonnaise awaits at your Club.

Now playing at the bar in Miami: The Grove, a tequila-based drink that celebrates the magic of the region’s incredible mangos. One of dozens of varieties that thrive in South Florida, the mango featured in this cocktail is tree-ripened and hand-picked for optimal flavor. It pairs beautifully with a hit of Thai Chili and Lime. 

PS: We love this cocktail so much that you can now find it at all MFG restaurants in Miami.

Upstairs at Privato, Mario and team reimagine Whole Tempura Crab with a Carbone-style spin—stuffed with a delicate farce of crab, scallop, and herbs, and paired with lemon agrumato aioli, spring garlic, and tomato. Refined, vibrant, and a joy to eat.

We'd like to introduce our Members in New York to the cocktail that Head of Bars Nathan O’Neill is calling “the drink of the summer” — The Aperol Sour. In this take on the classic aperitivo, lemon juice sharpness the profile of the Aperol, with an egg white finish creating the silkiest texture. It’s the perfect thing to sip on a sunny day.

The Caviar & Tomato returns to ZZ's — our seasonal take on the signature Caviar & Avocado. A whole cured heirloom tomato filled with bluefin tuna and yuzu crème fraîche, finished with Black Diamond Golden Ossetra Caviar.

Now playing at the bar at ZZ’s Club in Miami: The Division Bell, a smoky, vibrant, Mezcal-inspired standout that was first popularized at the legendary Lower East Side bar Mayahuel. Our version highlights the beautiful character of Siete Misterios’ Doba-Yej Mezcal, with layers of bright citrus, orange peel, and dark cherry from Aperol and maraschino liqueur.

Meet the cocktail of the summer, now playing at all of our restaurants in Miami: The Grove. It’s an irresistible celebration of the array of incredible mangoes that thrive in Florida, featuring Chinola Mango, Cazadores Blanco, Orange, Lime, and Aperol we infuse with Thai chili for a subtle hit of sultry heat.

The sweetest send-off: Ice Cream Sandos at ZZ’s Club 💌
